newsitem.title: POLAND: ABB raises stakes in three Polish firms.
newsitem.headline: ABB raises stakes in three Polish firms.

text.p: Engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG has increased stakes in its three Polish companies to nearly 100 percent by buying their shares from a treasury-owned agency for 125 million zlotys, ABB said on Wednesday.

ABB, which controls 12 firms in Poland, said in a statement the Industrial Development Agency (ARP) had sold it stakes in ABB Zamech, based in the northen city of Elblag, ABB Dolmel and Dolmel Drives, based in the south-western city of Wroclaw.
ARP has retained "a golden share" in the three companies, which allows it to influence strategic decisions.
ABB has so far held 76 percent of shares in ABB Zamech, 67 percent in ABB Dolmel and 20 percent in Dolmel Drives.

Out of the 125 million zlotys ABB has paid for the stakes, 50 million will go directly to Poland's central budget and the rest will be used to create an investment fund which will help state-owned firms undergoing restructuring, PAP news agency quoted ARP president Arkadiusz Krezel as saying.
ABB's Polish subsidiaries, employing 6,270 people, received orders worth about one billion zlotys last year, ABB said.
